  {"slot": 1, "score": 0.10, "why": "Nationwide 14-year criminalisation, death penalty under northern Sharia, predatory police extortion for 'looking gay', mass venue raids, app-based blackmail gangs, and an unprosecuted trans killing with official misgendering."},
  {"slot": 2, "score": 0.18, "why": "New penal code criminalises all same-sex relations; president's decree frames LGBTQ+ as national-defense threat; vigilante mobs attacking trans women, villa raids, caning province, dating-app bans, and a trans traveller dead in custody."},
  {"slot": 3, "score": 0.70, "why": "Self-declaration recognition, hate-crime and hate-speech bans, marriage equality, working courts recognising hate motive, welcoming travel guidance. Downsides are dating-app ambush robberies and high harassment prevalence — real but with functioning recourse."},
  {"slot": 4, "score": 0.30, "why": "Birth-sex prison placement with documented abuse, police non-cooperation, gangs extorting LGBT people, hospitals denying care, and a survey finding 85% accepting attacks on trans people — tempered by hate-crime law and a landmark police-conviction."},

**Dossier 1:** National criminalization of same-sex conduct (14 years), Sharia death penalty in 12 northern states, police extortion targeting those who "look gay", mass hotel raids, trans woman killed with impunity, dating app luring/blackmail gangs, no legal protections, foreign travel advisory warning attacks/blackmail. Death penalty risk under Sharia. This is severe. Trans-specific: police lever used against gender-nonconforming (the "looked gay" extortion is a police lever against presentation), app blackmail pattern, impunity for trans killing. Criminalization is enforced. This is severe — around 0.10–0.15. Death penalty only for male sodomy under Sharia in north, but a trans visitor outed could face the sodomy law risk (per rule 2, this matters when used as police lever against visibly gender-nonconforming — documented). So very low: ~0.12.

**Dossier 2:** New penal code criminalizing extra-marital sex (all same-sex relations, up to 2 years), Aceh caning, vigilante mobs attacking trans women escalating tied to presidential decree framing LGBTQ as national defense threat (state threat-framing, 2025), villa raid 75 arrested June 2025, death in custody of trans traveler (foreign student, allegations of beating, $100k ransom demand), censorship of apps (dating app banned), psychiatric pathologization, no legal protections, capital agency raids trans women as "socially dysfunctional," conversion therapy. State framing as national-defense threat + vigilante mobs surge + raids. Severe, but no death penalty. Trans traveler died in custody. ~0.18–0.22. Organized/state-tolerated targeting: vigilante mobs with official rhetoric. Aceh caning. I'd say ~0.20.

**Dossier 3:** Self-determination LGR (resident), hate crime/hate speech protections, marriage equality, conversion therapy ban, travel guide "safest and welcoming." Downsides: dating-app trap pattern (robbery/assault pattern targeting LGBT, documented rising), 90% harassment in capital region, equality bodies report rising violence, 35% of discrimination cases involved physical assault. No trans-specific homicide documented. Criminalization long repealed (1795). This is Reduced Risk to Low Risk. The dating-app ambush pattern is a real traveler-facing exposure (travelers use apps). But recourse exists, hate motive recognized in court, protections. ~0.70–0.75. The harassment prevalence is high though (90% verbal/psychological harassment in capital). That's social friction mostly. Dating app traps → robberies. I'd say 0.72.

**Dossier 4:** No gender identity law, no LGR (resident gap — not to be deducted for visitor unless documents doubted — dossier says foreign documents have "no domestic mechanism through which those documents could be aligned or challenged" — neutral). Hate crime law covering GI (3-6 years), enhanced penalty for bias killing (30-60 years), 2018 policy allowing complaints, first conviction of three police officers for killing a trans woman (20 years each — positive enforcement). But: 2013 survey — 85% believe it acceptable to attack a transgender individual; 500 hate crimes 1998-2015; police refusal to cooperate in LGBT death investigations; gang violence targeting LGBT with extortion; prison conditions hostile (birth-sex placement, forced shaving, punishment drills, HIV clinic denial during state of exception); hospital discrimination. The state of exception mass raids holding trans women in ordinary prison with no accommodation — tier 1/tier 2 exposure but applies in exception regime since March 2022 (ongoing?). Documented: 85% acceptance of attacking trans people is a huge societal hostility signal — but that's a 2013 survey (rule 18: dated). Still, IHRO 2020/2021 says fails to address violence. Police refusal to cooperate — but also a successful hate-crime conviction of police officers (2020).

Prevalence of violence: 500 hate crimes over 17 years ≈ 30/year — need denominator, unknown country size. The 85% figure about attacking trans individuals is a severe hostility signal, dated 2013.

Score: society extremely hostile, gangs target LGBT, police complicit, prison custody exposure under exception regime. But there's functioning hate-crime law with a real conviction. Overall: High risk — maybe 0.30–0.35.

**Dossier 5:** Constitutional court struck sterilization requirement, regional court found Art 8 violation, anti-discrimination law covers GI (2009), hate crimes recorded/prosecuted/sentenced, same-sex partnerships equal to marriage, supreme administrative court safeguard for detained trans foreigners, but prison placement unresolved/prisons unprepared, official hostility at highest level (head of state "these transgenders truly disgust me," justice minister), 43% discriminated/harassed (highest among trans), 51% targeted by insults/assault/threats, politicians' anti-LGBT speech 71%, constitutional ban on same-sex marriage moving with 80-90% of seats, far-right leaflets. Travel guide rates cities high. Discrimination prevalence at scale (43%/51% over 5 years, trans highest) — that's an everyday exposure signal per rule 21, tier with universal exposure. But functioning institutions, prosecutions, protections.

No criminalization. Official hostility is rhetoric (threat-framing but not state-imposed universal exposure). Prison placement unresolved — but visitor rarely imprisoned. Detention placement safeguard exists at supreme court level but inconsistent practice.

~0.60–0.68. Discrimination prevalence at scale plus hostile rhetoric pushes down; strong legal protections and enforcement push up. I'd say 0.64.

Ranking: 3 (0.72) > 5 (0.64) > 4 (0.32) > 2 (0.20) > 1 (0.12).

Let me finalize Dossier 1: is it lower than 2? Dossier 1 has death penalty (Sharia north, male sodomy), enforced criminalization nationwide, police extortion of gender-nonconforming, mass raids, impunity for trans killing, app blackmail gangs. Dossier 2 has 2-year national statute (selective), Aceh caning, vigilante mobs surge with state defense framing, trans traveler died in custody, capital raids of trans women. Both very bad. Dossier 1's death penalty + nationwide 14-year statute + documented predatory enforcement → 0.10. Dossier 2 → 0.18. Actually dossier 2's state framing (LGBT as national defense threat) plus vigilante surge is organized targeting tier. Dossier 1 also has that via weaponized law. I'll go 0.10 and 0.18.

Dossier 4: check tier-1 features: prison placement by birth sex with documented abuse in state of exception — applies to a visitor who is arrested. Hospitals dismiss trans patients, deny care — visitor could face that. 85% survey accepting attacking trans people (2013, dated but huge). Police refusal to cooperate. Hate-crime framework with conviction. I'll go 0.30.

Dossier 3: dating-app trap pattern with physical assault in 35% of cases — traveler-facing (apps used abroad). Rising violence/intimidation. But strong legal protections, hate motive convictions, no criminalization, welcoming travel guide. 0.70.

Final: 1: 0.10, 2: 0.18, 3: 0.70, 4: 0.30, 5: 0.64.
